stem: Priya's mother mixes a spoonful of curd into two bowls of milk. Bowl 1 has warm milk; bowl 2 has milk straight from the refrigerator. After five hours, only bowl 1 has set into firm curd. What is the best reason for this difference?

options.text: The bacteria in the starter grow and multiply faster at warm temperatures, so they turn the milk into curd quickly.
Cold milk contains fewer nutrients, so the bacteria in the starter cannot use it.
Warmth kills all the harmful microorganisms in the milk, allowing curd to form.
The refrigerator adds extra water to the milk, which stops curd from setting.

teacher.key_rationale: Lactobacillus in the curd starter multiplies rapidly at lukewarm (optimum) temperatures and converts milk to curd; low temperature slows microbial growth, so the cold bowl does not curdle in the same way. Only option A states this correctly.
